## Manual release steps

The automated release script (`release.ps1`) is convenient, but manual testing and execution provide the essential baseline and fallback in case any step fails or requires intervention.

::: {.callout-important}

Always perform manual sanity checks and test builds before running the automated release script.

:::

### Preliminary verification

Before bumping versions or creating releases, verify that all test suites and builds pass cleanly:

```bash
# Check Rust compilation sanity:
cargo check

# Run Python test suite:
uv sync --all-extras
uv run pytest -v

# Verify standalone C/C++ library build:
make -C src -n
```

### Update package version

Majordome versions are managed across `pyproject.toml` and `Cargo.toml`. Use [`uv version`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/package/#updating-your-version) and `cargo-set-version` to keep them synchronized:

```bash
# Install cargo-set-version if not yet available:
cargo install cargo-set-version

# Dry-run version bump to inspect the target version:
uv version --bump patch --dry-run  # or: minor, major

# Apply the version bump in pyproject.toml:
uv version --bump patch

# Synchronize Cargo.toml with the bumped version:
cargo set-version $(uv version --short)
```

On Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
$version = (uv version --short)
cargo set-version $version
```

### Build release wheels

Clean the `dist/` folder and build release wheels for Windows and Linux:

```bash
# Clean dist directory:
rm -rf dist/
mkdir -p dist/

# Build Windows wheel (when running on Windows):
uv build --wheel

# Build manylinux wheel with Cantera support using the container:
./release.sh
```

Inspect the generated wheel contents to ensure all required binaries, metadata, and shared libraries are bundled:

```bash
python -m zipfile -l dist/*.whl
```

### Commit and tag release

Commit version changes and create the git release tag:

```bash
git add Cargo.toml pyproject.toml Cargo.lock uv.lock
git commit -m "Release version $(uv version --short)"
git tag "v$(uv version --short)"
git push origin main --tags
```

On Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
git add Cargo.toml pyproject.toml Cargo.lock uv.lock
git commit -m "Release version $version"
git tag "v$version"
git push origin main --tags
```

### Build and publish documentation

Build documentation using Quarto and publish to GitHub Pages:

```bash
# Compile documentation:
uv run majordome-build-qmd --extras docs

# Publish rendered HTML to gh-pages branch:
quarto publish gh-pages --no-render --no-prompt --no-browser docs
```

### Create GitHub release

Publish the release with attached wheel artifacts using the GitHub CLI:

```bash
gh release create "v$(uv version --short)" dist/*.whl --generate-notes
```

### Publish to PyPI

Owners can publish the generated wheels to PyPI with `uv`:

```bash
uv publish
```
